newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction loans rise in May.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction loans rise in May.

text.p: Loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms grew by 0.8 percent to T$404.230 billion year on year in May, marking the first rise in two years, the central bank said on Friday.
The figure had gradually recovered since it fell 20.66 percent year-on-year in September 1996. This indicates a gradual bottoming-out of the real estate market, the bank said in a statement.
In a wider picture, loans extended by Taiwan banks to all private businesses rose a scant 1.11 percent to T$2.983 trillion in May from a year ago, the bank added.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has seen deep recession since the local property market peaked in 1989.
In August 1996, the central bank scrapped all the selective credit controls on land to boost the property market and the economy, and analysts had expected the move to gradually take effect.
Taiwan's gross domestic product rose 6.83 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997, up from 6.62 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
